title: The cards of power
subtitle: In which the thrones settle the visit, Hormuz is refused, Lavrov and Wadephul shake hands, and Paris fills the square.

body:
Yesterday a plan lay on the table. Today the refusal lies beside it. Between the two, in New York, two men shake hands who have not sat together in four years, and in Paris a square fills that once belonged to the Revolution.

I. Eight points, one refusal

Beijing tallies the visit in eight points: tariff cuts of thirty billion dollars on unsensitive goods, a trade council, a channel for incidents involving artificial intelligence. Next round in November; APEC in Shenzhen, the G20 in Miami. The great files stay blunt. The two thrones have drawn closer without exchanging blades. 1 2

In the Gulf comes the answer Saturday left open. Trump rejects the seven-day plan in front of the White House. He remains willing to talk, not on these terms. Araghchi waits for the mediators' official voice. The tankers wait longer than the diplomats. 5 6

II. Twenty minutes

Johann Wadephul and Sergey Lavrov sit at one table. Barely twenty minutes. Wadephul warns against the path taken against Germany, Europe and NATO and asks for grain routes across the Black Sea. Lavrov says afterwards he heard nothing new; they could have read him the statement over the phone. A handshake. The hall stays bright, and so does the cold. 3

China's vice-president Han Zheng urges that the postwar order be kept. In the field the handshake changes nothing. Trump publicly tells Zelenskyy to come to terms with Putin. 4 7

III. The square that fills

In Paris, by estimates, seven to eight hundred thousand people stand on the Place de la Concorde. Leo XIV rides the avenue in an open car. He speaks of the thirst for truth and peace, and of machines that must serve the human being, not dominion. Then Lourdes. 8

The chronicler's close

Three cards lie open: a refused calendar in the Gulf, a cold handshake in New York, a full square in Paris. Whether Tehran lays down a new hand belongs to the next leaf.
